raw_response:
I'm 74 years old. I've farmed these same 3 mu in Quzhou for fifty years, and I know every inch of this soil. It's just me and my wife now — our children left for the city long ago. We get by on what we grow and a little cash from selling the surplus. Right now it's early October. We just spent three long days pulling the summer maize by hand — small plot, so no need for machines, though my back complains more than it used to. The stalks are drying by the house. Next week the winter wheat has to go in, or we'll miss the window.

I save my own wheat seed every year. For 3 mu there's no sense paying for new seed — I've been selecting from the best heads for decades, and it works. Before planting, I'll hire my nephew's small tractor to plow and harrow the field — 80 yuan for the whole plot, which saves my back and gets it done in one morning. I'll broadcast about 35 kg of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind — as base fertilizer. The extension agent says I should use more, but fertilizer prices have gone up and I need to keep cash in hand for my wife's blood pressure medicine. In late March, when the wheat is at jointing, I'll topdress with 15 kg of urea per mu if the plants look a bit yellow. That gives me roughly 12 kg of nitrogen per mu total — not pushing for maximum yield, but enough to get 380 kg/mu if the weather cooperates, and I won't go broke doing it.

For water, I'll irrigate three times for the wheat: once after planting if the soil stays dry, once at green-up in March, and once during grain filling in May. Pumping from the well costs money — about 10 yuan per mu each time — but dry wheat is a disaster I can't afford. I'll spray herbicide in spring if the weeds look bad; usually once is enough.

Come June, the wheat comes off — I'll hire two days of help for the harvest because at our age we can't cut and thresh fast enough before the rains come. Immediately after, the maize goes in. For maize I buy hybrid seed — just 2 kg per mu, about 40 yuan — because the yield gain is worth it for summer crop. I put down 30 kg of compound per mu at planting, then side-dress 12 kg of urea when the plants are knee-high in July. Maize gets one good irrigation in July if the summer rains don't come through, and I'll spray herbicide once. If the armyworms show up like they did three years ago, I'll add insecticide too. We harvest the maize by hand in late September — another four or five days of work — and then the cycle starts again.

All told, I need about 1,460 yuan for inputs and hired labor this year. That's a lot for us, but it's less than what I'd lose from a bad yield. I expect about 380 kg/mu of wheat and 400 kg/mu of maize. Not much, but it keeps us in flour and brings a little cash. At my age, stability matters more than trying something new.
